name: adv_meta_maml_bad
title: MAML-style meta-learning with an inner and an outer loop - five planted defects
origin: written for the domain-generative-rl-graph hardening round, 2026-09-13
note: The outer loop iterates a DataLoader, so unlike adv_ppo_bad the MLV2xx family can see it and MLV201 fires. The three meta-learning defects - no second-order graph, support and query drawn from the same slice, and an inner loop whose manual SGD never zeroes anything - have no rule and are recorded under `unsupported`.

expected.why: every meta-update is the running sum of every task seen so far, so the meta-parameters diverge within a few hundred iterations
MetaLearner carries two BatchNorm2d layers and a Dropout, so the held-out tasks are scored with dropout active and the running statistics are updated by the test batches

expected.defect: meta_test() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: a full autograd graph is built over every held-out task and discarded

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path and stops loading when the file moves

forbidden.why: the training task loader is built with shuffle=True at line 114
the test task loader is built with shuffle=False at line 116
both loaders are constructed inside main(), which runs only under the if __name__ == "__main__" guard, and num_workers is not set
meta_loss.backward() at line 86 precedes meta_optimizer.step() at line 87
there is no no_grad block in this file, so backward cannot be inside one
nothing accumulates a loss across iterations; meta_loss.item() is only printed
the inner adaptation loop is part of training and legitimately needs gradients - torch.autograd.grad is called on its loss at line 70
MetaLearner.forward returns the raw head output; no softmax precedes either cross_entropy
images and labels are moved to DEVICE at the top of both loops (lines 78-79 and 99-100)
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 20
the task sets are cut by index slice, not by a randomised splitter
MetaLearner.__init__ calls super().__init__() on its first line
features and head are plain attributes; the `weights` list at line 66 holds tensors from .parameters(), not submodule constructions

unsupported.defect: create_graph is False, so the adapted weights carry no graph back to the meta-parameters and MAML silently degrades to its first-order approximation
unsupported.why: no rule models the second-order requirement of a meta-learning inner loop.

unsupported.symbol: support = slice(0, N_WAY * K_SHOT); query = slice(0, N_WAY * K_SHOT)
unsupported.defect: the support and query halves are the same slice, so every query example was already adapted on
unsupported.why: MLV101/MLV102 model an sklearn transformer fitted on the wrong rows; two identical index slices inside a task splitter is the same leak in an idiom no rule covers.

unsupported.defect: the inner loop takes its gradients with torch.autograd.grad and rebinds a local list, so nothing in it is wrong today - but a reader looking for `the inner loop never zeroes` gets no answer either way
unsupported.why: MLV201 anchors on a loop over a LOADER-tagged value; the inner adaptation loop iterates range(INNER_STEPS) and is invisible to it.
